currentContext.expansion: Tourism Finance Corporation of India Limited (TFCI) operates as a specialized non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on lending to the tourism, hospitality, and broader infrastructure sectors. The company's expansion strategy is centered on diversifying its loan portfolio while maintaining a core focus on hospitality and tourism. Key expansion plans include: (1) Financing greenfield projects, last-mile funding for projects under implementation, brownfield projects, takeover/refinancing opportunities, acquisition finance, corporate finance, structured finance, and special situation funding. (2) Actively pursuing lending opportunities in resilient sectors such as manufacturing, healthcare, education, renewable energy, social infrastructure, warehousing, logistics, and real estate, with particular emphasis on affordable and middle-income residential housing. (3) Extending lending for onward financing to NBFCs, HFCs, and ARCs, and exploring opportunities in structured credit, special situation credit, loan against property, and lending against listed securities. (4) Engaging in joint-lending and/or co-lending arrangements with banks and established NBFCs for secured MSE and LAP products. (5) Undertaking fee-based activities in areas such as tourism advisory, corporate advisory, and loan syndication. (6) Adopting a measured diversification strategy by committing to invest up to Rs.90 crore in Category-II Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) registered with SEBI to provide structured and growth-oriented credit/capital to hospitality, real-estate, and diverse sectors. (7) The company may raise funds through the issue of long-term bonds/debentures depending on the emerging interest rate scenario, with shareholder approval sought for private placement of non-convertible bonds/debentures up to Rs.1200 crore.

It also extends credit to manufacturing, social/urban infrastructure, real estate, and other NBFCs/HFCs/ARCs, while undertaking fee-based advisory and loan syndication services.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian economy expected to maintain strong growth momentum, transitioning to an investment and productivity-led economy with average annual GDP growth normalizing between 6.5%-7%.
- Tourism and hospitality sector well-positioned for sustained growth driven by favourable demographics, increasing disposable incomes, and expanding connectivity.
- Branded hotel demand-supply gap of around 8-9% with sustained demand and healthy operating performance across the organised hospitality sector.
- Government infrastructure capex increased to Rs.12.22 lakh crore, reinforcing infrastructure-led long-term economic growth and balanced urban development.
- Renewable energy, healthcare, and education sectors witnessing steady growth and offering ample financing opportunities.
- Real estate sector expected to grow at 9.63% CAGR in next five years, with residential segment continuing as backbone of growth, though moderation in residential sales volume observed in Q4FY2026.
- Branded hotel development pipeline and signings expanded to an aggregate about 1.11 lakh rooms in the last two years, with about 0.76 lakh room signings expected in CY2026.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Actively provide financial assistance through term loans to infrastructure projects in renewable energy, healthcare, education and other resilient infra sub-segments.
- Focus on construction finance opportunities in real estate with risk mitigation and structured financial controls.
- The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs.0.60 per equity share (30% on paid-up capital) for FY2026, subject to shareholder approval. The Company has a Dividend Distribution Policy, and dividend is paid to members on record date. No public deposits were invited or outstanding. The Company prioritizes continuous monitoring of its resource base to optimize funding strategy and raise funds from diversified sources to enhance the weighted average cost of funds.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Tourism Finance Corporation of India Limited (TFCI) operates as a specialized non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on lending to the tourism, hospitality, and broader infrastructure sectors. The company's expansion strategy is centered on diversifying its loan portfolio while maintaining a core focus on hospitality and tourism. Key expansion plans include: (1) Financing greenfield projects, last-mile funding for projects under implementation, brownfield projects, takeover/refinancing opportunities, acquisition finance, corporate finance, structured finance, and special situation funding. (2) Actively pursuing lending opportunities in resilient sectors such as manufacturing, healthcare, education, renewable energy, social infrastructure, warehousing, logistics, and real estate, with particular emphasis on affordable and middle-income residential housing. (3) Extending lending for onward financing to NBFCs, HFCs, and ARCs, and exploring opportunities in structured credit, special situation credit, loan against property, and lending against listed securities. (4) Engaging in joint-lending and/or co-lending arrangements with banks and established NBFCs for secured MSE and LAP products. (5) Undertaking fee-based activities in areas such as tourism advisory, corporate advisory, and loan syndication. (6) Adopting a measured diversification strategy by committing to invest up to Rs.90 crore in Category-II Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) registered with SEBI to provide structured and growth-oriented credit/capital to hospitality, real-estate, and diverse sectors. (7) The company may raise funds through the issue of long-term bonds/debentures depending on the emerging interest rate scenario, with shareholder approval sought for private placement of non-convertible bonds/debentures up to Rs.1200 crore.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 37-year track record and deep specialization in tourism/hospitality financing, having funded 30% of India's star-category hotel room supply (59,000 rooms).
- Strong asset quality with Net NPA of 0% and Gross NPA of 0.37% as of March 2026, supported by a strict appraisal and proactive monitoring framework.
- High capital adequacy of 55.53% and low gearing of 0.83 times, providing a strong base for growth and risk absorption.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Credit Risk — Arises from borrower/counterparty default, especially in project lending where implementation delays and cost overruns are common in developing economies. TFCI mitigates via Board-approved Credit Policy, sensitivity analysis, and intensive project monitoring.
- Operational Risk — Loss from inadequate internal processes, people, systems, or external events. TFCI manages through strong internal controls, segregation of duties, dual-check authorization, and is implementing RBI's guidance note on operational resilience.
- Interest Rate Risk — Mismatches between interest-rate-sensitive assets and liabilities. Mitigated by aligning lending rates with average cost of borrowings and monitoring asset-liability maturity patterns.
- Liquidity Risk — Inability to meet obligations as they become due. Managed via short-term liquidity forecasts, immediate gap correction, diversified funding sources, and strong capital adequacy.
- Compliance & Regulatory Risk — Risk of sanctions, financial loss, or reputational damage from non-compliance with laws and regulations. Mitigated through a senior management-monitored framework and inter-departmental coordination.
